content.tldr: An offset is a 64-bit integer that uniquely identifies the sequential position of a message within a specific partition, providing order and enabling consumer progress tracking.
content.simple_explanation: When a producer writes a message to a partition, Kafka assigns it a sequential, immutable integer offset starting at 0. Offsets are strictly local to a partition (offset 42 in partition 0 has no relation to offset 42 in partition 1). Consumers maintain an offset pointer indicating the next record they intend to read. Offsets decouple consumers from brokers: multiple consumers can read from different offsets concurrently without locking or deleting records.
content.real_world_example: A numbered ticket dispenser at a bakery counter: every arriving customer pulls ticket #101, #102, #103; the server calls the next ticket number sequentially, and anyone can look at the counter display to see exactly what number is being served.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Offsets cannot provide total global ordering across an entire topic with multiple partitions; Kafka guarantees strict FIFO message ordering exclusively within a single partition.
